claims.statement: `create_deep_agent` structurally routes `graph_id` specs to remote asynchronous subagents, `runnable` specs to caller-owned compiled subagents, and other specs to declarative subagents compiled for the inline `task` tool.

SubAgentMiddleware exposes one `task` tool selected by named subagent; it rejects duplicate names during construction, returns an error for unknown types, and requires a tool-call ID to return a parent-state command.

Ordinary inline task delegation is stateless: it strips messages, todos, structured response, the fork marker, and private middleware state from the parent and invokes the child with one HumanMessage containing the delegation description.

The inline task path relies on LangGraph's ambient per-key configuration merge for parent callbacks, tags, and configurable values, adds only the `ls_agent_type="subagent"` tracing marker, and returns compatible non-private state updates together with a ToolMessage.

Task results prefer JSON serialization of a non-null structured response and otherwise extract the last non-empty AIMessage text; a compiled runnable must return a state containing `messages` or the middleware raises ValueError.

Declarative subagents inherit model, tools, and filesystem permissions unless overridden; provided permissions replace parent rules, first matching rules win, and builder middleware starts with filesystem, summarization, and patching, adding skills when declared before applying profile and custom middleware machinery.

The builder auto-adds the `general-purpose` declarative subagent with parent model, tools, permissions, and a default stack unless the harness profile disables it or a supplied inline agent already has that name.

Raw declarative specs support declared and per-task dynamic response formats via `__deepagents_subagent_response_format`; the dynamic override recompiles the raw spec and is rejected for compiled runnable entries.

Experimental fork mode builds inherited effective history by applying the parent's summarization event and adding a task preamble; declarative forks rebuild the inherited prompt and state, cannot declare skills, while opaque compiled forks omit private state, and the fork marker prevents recursive task delegation.

AsyncSubAgentMiddleware launches Agent Protocol work through LangGraph SDK threads and runs, immediately persists and returns a task ID, and supplies check, update, cancel, and list tools; updating interrupts the current run and creates a replacement on the same remote thread.

Async task records are merged by task ID in `async_tasks` state, retaining remote thread/run IDs and timestamps across compaction; clients are lazy cached by URL and headers, and url-less ASGI transport requires an asynchronous parent invocation.

SkillsMiddleware progressively discloses skills by injecting names, descriptions, annotations, and SKILL.md paths into the system prompt while directing the model to read full instructions only when applicable.

Skill loading uses backend listing and download APIs, parses SKILL.md YAML metadata defensively, skips malformed, inaccessible, non-UTF8, and oversized candidates with warnings, and resolves same-named skills from ordered sources using last-one-wins precedence.

Skills metadata and recoverable source errors are private state and are loaded once before an agent session unless `skills_metadata` already exists; templates require skills locations, warnings, and list slots, while `system_prompt=None` suppresses only prompt injection.
`isolated` is the default subagent mode, while `handoff` is accepted as a legacy alias for it; only `fork` receives inherited parent context, and unsupported modes fail validation.
Async task listing filters by cached status before refreshing selected nonterminal runs; terminal statuses are not queried, and failed live lookups preserve the cached status.

Talon loads remote async-subagent definitions from `[async_subagents.<name>]` TOML tables and supplies the loader to its `DeepAgentRuntime`; a missing file yields no definitions, while unreadable, malformed, or invalid configuration fails closed rather than starting with only valid entries.

Talon compiles local `AGENTS.md` subagents as fresh task-only agents with optional exact tool attachments and applicable approval policy; it rejects SDK fork mode and lets a task add, but not replace, configured tools on a named local subagent.

Talon's `BackgroundSubagents` detaches inline and remote delegation into bounded in-memory workers scoped to a conversation, uses distinct job thread IDs, and delivers completed non-cancelled results to a later owning main-agent turn before acknowledgement.

Talon's explicit `reload_subagent_configuration` validates and replaces the graph for subsequent turns while preserving active turns and background tasks on their original capabilities; a failed reload leaves the previous agents active.

Talon background workers clear the authorization handler and disable operator approval; protected inline or remote work reports an unmet approval instead of awaiting an approval interaction after the originating turn.

Talon result delivery is owner-scoped and retry-aware: completed results are acknowledged after a main turn, can be requeued when the host discards that turn's reply, and are dropped after three failed processing turns; failures and timeouts yield distinct safe result text.
